pinterest.title: Wedding Morning Timeline Worked Back From Your Ceremony
pinterest.description: A wedding morning timeline is built backwards from the ceremony: fix the time you leave, then when you must be dressed, then when the photographer arrives, and start the first hair and makeup chair early enough to finish everyone before that. For a 4pm ceremony, for example, that can mean hair and makeup from 9am with a first look or from 10am without one. Every time is an example to adapt with your stylist and artist.

pinterest.title: Wedding Morning Timeline and Who Sits First in the Chairs
pinterest.description: The order of the hair and makeup chairs shapes the whole wedding morning. Start with anyone who has to leave early, anyone with the simplest look and anyone whose hair needs time to set. The person getting married finishes last or close to last, so their makeup is freshest for the photos. Some teams prefer second to last, so an overrun falls on someone else. Ask your stylist and artist which order suits them.

pinterest.title: Wedding Morning Schedule Template to Copy, Filled From the Ceremony Up
pinterest.description: A wedding morning schedule template to copy into a document or spreadsheet. Fill it from the bottom up, starting with the ceremony: out of sight as guests arrive, leave for the ceremony, first look, dressed and ready, a buffer before dressing, the last chair, the photographer's arrival for details, a row for each person's hair and makeup, the first chair, and suite access and breakfast. Give a copy to your team and your timekeeper.

slides: Planning your wedding morning? Don't start with hair and makeup. Start with the ceremony time and work backwards.
Work back in this order: the ceremony, travel to it, photos before it, dressed and ready, then the chairs. The first chair's start is the last number you work out.
An example for a 4pm ceremony with a first look: hair and makeup from 9am, photographer at 12.30pm for details, dressed and ready at 1.45pm, first look at 2pm. Times to adapt, not rules.
Without a first look, for example: hair and makeup from 10am, photographer at 1.30pm, dressed at 2.30pm, out of sight at 3.30pm as guests arrive.
Chair order: anyone leaving early or with the simplest look goes first. The person getting married finishes last or close to last, so their makeup is freshest for the photos.
How long each chair takes is a question for your stylist and artist. Time your trial, ask for their figures in writing and build the morning on them.
Put the buffer at the handovers: before the dress goes on, before you leave for the ceremony and around a first look.

instagram_carousel.caption:
A wedding morning is built backwards from the ceremony. Fix the time you leave, then the time you must be dressed, then when the photographer arrives, and only then work out when the first hair and makeup chair begins.

Our new guide sets out two example mornings for a 4pm ceremony. With a first look, hair and makeup might begin at 9am. Without one, it might begin at 10am. Every time in it is an example to adapt: your own start depends on the number of people in the chairs and the pace your stylist and artist give you.

How long each person takes in the chair depends on the look, the hair and the person, so time your trial and ask your team for their figures in writing.

The guide also covers who sits first and last, when the photographer should arrive, where the buffer belongs, setting up the getting ready space, how the morning moves for 2pm, 3pm and 5pm ceremonies, questions to ask a destination venue about heat, the suite and the walk to the ceremony, and a morning schedule template to copy.

Planning a wedding morning at a destination venue? A Wedded Advisor works in your time zone and is your single point of contact for the venue questions. Start the conversation with Wedded Concierge.

Read the full guide via the link in our bio.

newsletter.preview: When hair and makeup start, who sits last, when the photographer arrives and where the buffer goes.
newsletter.blurb: Your wedding morning starts with the ceremony time, not the first chair. Our new guide works back from it: when to be dressed, when the photographer arrives for details, the order of the hair and makeup chairs and where the buffer belongs. It includes two example mornings for a 4pm ceremony, with and without a first look, how the morning moves for earlier and later ceremonies, questions to ask a destination venue and a schedule template to copy.
